text: The diagonal lemma (fixed-point lemma) guarantees that for any formula φ(x) with one free variable, there is a sentence ψ such that:
choices: T ⊢ ψ ↔ φ(⌜ψ⌝), i.e. ψ 'says' of itself that it has property φ
ψ is provable if and only if φ is a tautology
explanation: The diagonal lemma yields a self-referential ψ with T ⊢ ψ ↔ φ(⌜ψ⌝) — ψ asserts of its own Gödel number that φ holds. Applying it to ¬Provable(x) produces the Gödel sentence. Option A would make T inconsistent; options C and D misstate the lemma, which is about self-reference, not decidability or tautologousness.
